subject: Architecture
title: Tibetan Monastery Architecture: Building on Cliffsides
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tibetan Monastery Architecture: Building on Cliffsides usable.

hook.text: Tibetan monasteries cling to cliff faces at 15,000 feet — built in places that seem impossible to reach.

buildup.text: Tiger's Nest Monastery in Bhutan perches 10,000 feet above sea level on a sheer cliff face since 1692.

discovery.text: Thick mud-brick walls with small windows retain heat in extreme cold and block fierce Himalayan winds.

twist.text: Isolation was intentional. Monks built in unreachable places to focus on meditation away from worldly noise.

climax.text: The Potala Palace in Lhasa has 1,000 rooms stacked 13 stories high — the Dalai Lama's former winter home.

punchline.text: The harder the climb, the deeper the silence.

quiz.question: Why were Tibetan monasteries built in such remote locations?
options: To defend against military invasions from neighboring kingdoms
To isolate monks from worldly distractions for meditation
To access rare medicinal plants growing at high altitudes
